It is not a dead end: the GitHub MCP tool GITHUB_COMMIT_MULTIPLE_FILES (owner kavopdf, repo app, branch main, upserts=[{path,content,encoding:utf-8}]) commits several files atomically and worked for all four commits of this run. context: 041122's spill is now measured and its cause is named. The pending item asked for rendered row heights against declared trHeight: r2 +9.0, r19 +8.5, r20 +20.7, r23 +108.9, every other row exact. They grow by WHOLE LINES, not by a paragraph property - r23 has 20 source lines and rendered 26, its w:before sums to 24 pt and its w:line is exact 240 tw = the source's own 12 pt pitch. The extra lines are wraps: the docx names Effra, the renderer substitutes Noto Sans (16.9 % wider on the same string), and the cell gives the source's longest line 0.5 % of slack. Ruled out by measurement: w:before, w:line, w:cantSplit, the sizePt bug, the pieces index. Also disproved: our page 7 is NOT table 17 - it is page 6's page furniture (heading bar, footer rule, page number at y -7.5) whose anchor paragraphs were pushed off page 6; table 17 begins on our page 8. Second finding: building a metric clone of the source's own font from the PDF's /Widths arrays (installed to ~/.fonts) takes r2 to its declared 84.1 and r23 from 340.4 to 256.4 - the wrap theory confirmed - but the document still renders 12 pages, because the engine's own line box (240 tw = 12.0 pt) is taller than the pitch its own row height assumes (231.5 pt for 20 lines = 11.6 pt each). That 0.4 pt a line is the engine-side residual and it is the next thing to change. Nothing was committed to the engine this run: the font work is a harness measurement, not a fix, and a half-working font install would have moved the corpus without a mechanism.
